title: Tenant routing mismatch causing ledger siloing and partial credit writes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several enterprise customers reported recurring undercounts after regional failovers. We traced this to a routing mismatch where a subset of writes for token credits were accepted by a stale regional ledger replica (a 'silo') and never reconciled into the global rollup. The immediate trigger was a combination of (1) regional API gateway header rewrite under specific retry paths that dropped X-Redwood-Tenant when payloads exceeded a boundary, and (2) rapid leadership changes in the LedgerStore cluster that caused the write to be routed to a replica with a disabled cross-region replication flag. The result: partial credit writes that appeared successful to callers but were excluded from billing rollups, causing customer-visible undercounts and invoice deltas after failover and regional promotion.
reproduction_steps: 1) Configure a synthetic tenant with cross-region replication enabled and a long streaming request that triggers gateway retry (see test proxy config test-proxy/long-payload.yaml).
2) Force a leadership flip in LedgerStore (kubectl cordon + leader-election toggle) during an in-flight credit write.
3) Observe the API gateway logs: look for header rewrite events where X-Redwood-Tenant is absent for the retry leg.
4) Query regional ledger replica directly and global rollup: write appears in the regional silo but not in global aggregation within the expected window.
impact_summary: High-severity billing impact for a small number of enterprise tenants using multi-region routing and long-lived streaming calls. Customers saw undercounts ranging from 0.1% to 4% depending on workload shape and number of failovers during the billing window. This has triggered escalations with three accounts and a support SLA breach for one Dedicated customer.
mitigation_actions: 1) Temporary mitigation: Block gateway retry path that triggers header rewrite for tenants with cross-region replication (deployed 2025-09-19).
2) Manual reconciliation: backfill missing credits for impacted accounts using ledger diff tool (runbook: docs/runbooks/ledger-backfill.md).
3) Customer comms: notify affected accounts and set expectation for reconciliation timeline (support ticket IDs linked).
proposed_fix: Two-part fix: (A) harden the API gateway to preserve X-Redwood-Tenant across all retry paths and increase header buffer limits; (B) update LedgerStore leader-election to ensure writes during promotion are proxied to the global aggregator or buffered until replication confirmation. Implement idempotent write markers to detect and repair siloed writes during replication gaps.
rollback_plan: If gateway hardening causes regressions, revert the retry-path change and re-enable mitigation blocking, then reintroduce header preservation as a targeted patch. For LedgerStore changes, can revert to previous leader-election behavior and disable promotion automation for the short window.
qa_checks: Synthetic end-to-end test that simulates leader flip and verifies global rollup contains every accepted write (e2e/ledger/leader-flip-test).
Load test with long streaming payloads to validate gateway header preservation under retry and backpressure.
Integration test for idempotent write markers to ensure duplicate suppression and reconciliation work across regions.
postmortem_notes: Initial incident detection: Support ticket flagged unexplained invoice deltas 2025-09-17; SRE triaged and elevated to engineering 2025-09-18.
Root cause hypothesis validated by correlating gateway rewrite logs and LedgerStore replication tails 2025-09-19.
Planned postmortem will include timeline, telemetry gaps, and follow-up automation to detect siloed writes in real-time.
